dossier.title: Fixed limiter race condition
dossier.subtitle: Request counter was not shared across worker processes, allowing 4x the configured rate.

blocks.text: The rate limiter counted requests per process. With four workers, each worker had its own counter, so the service allowed four times the configured rate. The fix moves the counter to shared memory.
The fix is deployed to production. Requests are now properly rate limited.

pages.title: Technical details
pages.summary: How the race condition happened and how it was resolved.

blocks.text: Each worker process imported the limiter at startup, creating a fresh counter. The counter was a module-level variable, so no data was shared. The first request on any worker would see a zero counter and increment it locally.
We moved the counter to a Redis key. Every worker increments the same key and checks the same value. One Redis call per request is acceptable for the configured rate.
We ran load tests sending 1000 requests per second across four workers. With the old code, all 1000 were accepted. With the new code, the configured limit of 250 per second was enforced consistently.
